---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack API. Send, schedule, update, delete, and thread messages; post to channels and DMs; list channels, members, and conversation history; manage reactions, files, and status; and compose messages with mrkdwn and Block Kit. Use when the user wants to automate Slack notifications, read from or write to a Slack workspace, or build Slack messages programmatically via the Web API or incoming webhooks.
---

# Slack API

Interact with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API (`https://slack.com/api/<method>`) or incoming webhooks. Covers notifications, reads, and message composition. Node 18+ is required for the bundled script.

## Authentication

- Export the token before calling the API: `export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-...` (bot token) or `xoxp-...` (user token). `scripts/slack_request.cjs` and the examples below read `SLACK_TOKEN`.
- Send it as `Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN`. Incoming webhook URLs carry their own auth; do not attach a token to them.
- Bots need the app installed in the destination channel (`chat:write`); to post to any public channel without joining it, add the `chat:write.public` scope.
- Never print tokens, commit them, or embed them in Slack message content. If a call fails with `invalid_auth`, `missing_scope`, `not_in_channel`, or `channel_not_found`, surface the exact error and fix auth/membership before retrying.

## API conventions

- POST to `https://slack.com/api/<method>` with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` (form-encoded bodies are also accepted; GET with query params works for reads). UTF-8 is required for non-ASCII text and emoji.
- Every response is an envelope: `{"ok": true, ...}` on success or `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` on failure. Always check `ok`; treat `ok: false` as an error and quote the `error` string. Slack often returns HTTP 200 for API-level failures.
- Prefer IDs over display names. Resolve them first via `conversations.list` / `users.list` — never invent IDs.
- Rate limits: on HTTP 429, back off for the seconds in the `Retry-After` header. The default tier is roughly 1 request/second per method, and list-type reads are stricter. Retry transient `internal_error` / `service_unavailable` responses with backoff.
- Pagination: paged responses return `response_metadata.next_cursor`; pass it back as `cursor` and repeat until empty.

## Quick start

Send a message with curl:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello from the build pipeline"}'
```

List channels (GET style) and read history (POST style):

```bash
curl -sS "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?types=public_channel&limit=200" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"
curl -sS -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.history \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"C1234567890","limit":10}'
```

Or use the bundled client `scripts/slack_request.cjs` — deterministic JSON handling, automatic 429/5xx retry, and LLM-friendly output:

```bash
node scripts/slack_request.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello"}'
node scripts/slack_request.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel","limit":200}'
node scripts/slack_request.cjs conversations.history '{"channel":"C1234567890","limit":10}'
node scripts/slack_request.cjs users.lookupByEmail '{"email":"ada@example.com"}'
```

The script prints response JSON to stdout and exits `0` when `ok: true`, `1` on transport/HTTP failure, and `2` on usage/auth/config errors. If a method ever rejects a JSON body, fall back to curl with form fields: `curl -F channel=C1234567890 -F text=hi https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage`.

## Task map

- Send a notification or message → `chat.postMessage`; reply in a thread by adding the parent message's `ts` as `thread_ts`.
- Message visible to only one user → `chat.postEphemeral`.
- Read channels / DMs / members / history / threads → `conversations.list`, `conversations.members`, `conversations.history`, `conversations.replies`.
- Create, rename, archive channels → `conversations.create`, `conversations.rename`, `conversations.archive`.
- Identify users → `users.list`, `users.info`, `users.lookupByEmail`.
- Set a status, react to a message, attach a file → `users.profile.set`, `reactions.add`, `files.upload`.

Endpoint details, arguments, and scopes: load `references/methods.md`. Before composing messages with formatting, mentions, links, dates, or interactive blocks: load `references/formatting.md`.

## Guardrails

- Resolve channel/user IDs through the API before sending; never fabricate them.
- Re-read content and destination before posting anything real, and stay within the user's stated intent; when the target channel is ambiguous, ask.
- When using `blocks`, always pass a short `text` fallback (used by notifications and accessibility tooling).
- Check `ok` in every response; a readable `error` string beats a generic failure.

# Slack Web API — Methods Reference

Load this file when a task needs argument details, scopes, or response shapes for specific methods. Confirm edge cases against `https://api.slack.com/methods/<method>` — exact scope requirements depend on the app's configuration and workspace settings.

Contents
- [Messaging](#messaging)
- [Conversations](#conversations)
- [Users](#users)
- [Reactions](#reactions)
- [Files](#files)
- [Incoming webhooks](#incoming-webhooks)
- [Common errors](#common-errors)

## Messaging

### chat.postMessage
Send a message to a channel, DM, or thread.

- `channel` (ID preferred), plus `text` and/or `blocks`. When using `blocks`, keep `text` as a short fallback for notifications.
- `thread_ts` replies inside the thread of an existing message.
- Optional: `mrkdwn`, `link_names` (linkify @names), `unfurl_links`, `unfurl_media`, `username`, `icon_emoji`.
- Scope: `chat:write` (bot must be a member of the channel, or the app has `chat:write.public` for public channels).
- Returns `channel`, `ts` (message id — reuse as `thread_ts` for replies), `message`.

### chat.postEphemeral
Message visible only to one `user` inside `channel`. Same body options as postMessage. Scope: `chat:write`.

### chat.update
Edit an existing message: `channel` + `ts`, with new `text`/`blocks`. Only messages created by the same token can be edited. Scope: `chat:write`.

### chat.delete
Delete a message: `channel` + `ts`. Scope: `chat:write`.

### chat.scheduleMessage
Schedule a message: `channel`, `text`/`blocks`, and `post_at` (unix timestamp; Slack allows up to 120 days in advance). Returns `scheduled_message_id`. Scope: `chat:write`.

## Conversations

### conversations.list
Enumerate conversations. `types` is a comma-separated list of `public_channel`, `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im` (defaults to `public_channel`). Use `limit`, `cursor`, `exclude_archived: true`. Scopes: `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`. Returns `channels[]` with `id`, `name`, `is_private`, `is_member`.

### conversations.info
Look up one conversation by `channel`. Same read scopes. Returns the conversation object including `purpose` and `topic`.

### conversations.history
Recent messages: `channel`, plus optional `limit`, `cursor`, `oldest`, `latest` (unix timestamps), `inclusive`. Scopes: `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history`. Returns `messages[]`; each message has `ts`, `user`, `text`, and optional `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `reply_count`.

### conversations.replies
All messages in a thread: `channel` + `ts` of the parent message. Same history scopes. Returns the parent plus its replies.

### conversations.members
User IDs in a conversation: `channel`, plus `limit`/`cursor`. Read scopes as above. Resolve profiles separately with `users.info`, batching in small groups.

### conversations.create
Create a channel: `name` (no leading `#`, lowercase per Slack rules) and optional `is_private`. Scopes: `channels:manage` (public) / `groups:write` (private). Fails if a conversation with that name already exists.

### conversations.rename
Rename a conversation: `channel` + `name`. Scopes: `channels:manage` / `groups:write`.

### conversations.archive / unarchive
Archive or restore: `channel`. Scopes: `channels:manage` / `groups:write`. Posting to an archived channel fails with `is_archived`.

## Users

### users.list
List workspace members; paginate with `cursor`/`limit`. Scope: `users:read`. Can be slow in large workspaces — prefer `users.lookupByEmail` or `users.info` when you know the target.

### users.info
Profile for one user: `user`. Scope: `users:read`. Email is only returned when the token has `users:read.email` and workspace settings allow it.

### users.lookupByEmail
Resolve a user id from `email`. Scope: `users:read.email`.

### users.profile.set
Update profile fields, e.g. status:

```json
{"profile": {"status_text": "In a meeting", "status_emoji": ":calendar:", "status_expiration": 0}}
```

`status_expiration` is a unix timestamp; `0` means never expire. Clear a status with an empty `status_text`. Scope: `users.profile:write`.

## Reactions

### reactions.add
Add an emoji reaction to a message: `channel`, `name` (emoji shortcode without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), and `timestamp` (the message `ts`). Scope: `reactions:write`.

### reactions.remove
Remove a reaction added by the acting user: same arguments as add. Scope: `reactions:write`.

### reactions.get
List reactions on a message: `channel` + `timestamp`. Scope: `reactions:read`.

## Files

### files.upload (legacy)
Upload a file: `channels`, plus `content` (text) or an actual file via multipart form, `filename`, optional `initial_comment`. Scope: `files:write`. Legacy endpoint — for new code prefer the three-step flow `files.getUploadURLExternal` → PUT to the returned URL → `files.completeUploadExternal`.

## Incoming webhooks

- Purpose: post messages without a token; the webhook URL itself is the secret.
- POST JSON to the webhook URL: `{"text": "...", "blocks": [...]}` with optional `channel`, `username`, `icon_emoji` overrides.
- Responds with plain text `ok` on success; there is no response envelope and no read capability. Use the Web API for anything beyond fire-and-forget posting.

## Common errors

- `invalid_auth` — bad or revoked token.
- `missing_scope` — token lacks the required scope.
- `not_in_channel` — bot is not in the target channel (or needs `chat:write.public` for public channels).
- `channel_not_found` — bad channel ID or name.
- `is_archived` — posting to an archived channel.
- `invalid_blocks` / `invalid_arguments` — malformed payload; check the JSON structure.
- `too_many_requests` / HTTP 429 — rate limited; honor `Retry-After`.
- `internal_error` / `service_unavailable` — transient; retry with backoff.

# Formatting Slack Messages

Load this file before composing message `text` or Block Kit `blocks` payloads. Links and mentions require real IDs — resolve them through the API first.

## text vs blocks

- `text` — a plain string rendered as mrkdwn by default (`mrkdwn: true`). Good for simple messages.
- `blocks` — structured Block Kit JSON for rich messages (sections, dividers, buttons). When blocks are present, `text` becomes the fallback used by notifications and screen readers, so always include a short one.
- `plain_text` objects never render formatting; `mrkdwn` objects do.

## mrkdwn syntax

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, and `` ```preformatted``` `` for multi-line preformatted text.
- Emoji: `:wave:`, `:white_check_mark:`, etc.
- User mention: `<@U1234567890>`; channel link: `<#C1234567890|general>`.
- Broadcasts: `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>`, or a user group `<!subteam^S1234567890|eng>`.
- Links: `<https://example.com|Click here>`. Bare URLs are auto-linked by Slack.
- Dates from a unix timestamp with a fallback: `<!date^1699999999^{date_long} at {time}|never>`. Available tokens: `{date}`, `{date_long}`, `{date_short}`, `{date_pretty}`, `{date_short_pretty}`, `{time}`, `{time_secs}`.
- Escape `&`, `<`, `>` as `&`, `<`, `>` whenever they should appear literally (always escape user-supplied input).

## Block Kit essentials

Common block types: `section`, `divider`, `header`, `context`, `actions`, `image`; `input` is for modals only. Slack enforces limits (e.g. max 50 blocks per message, ~3000 characters per block text object) — check https://api.slack.com/reference/block-kit/blocks before pushing anything close to the edge.

Full message payload example (sections, fields, divider, actions):

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "text": "Deploy finished: v2.4.1 is live",
  "blocks": [
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": {
        "type": "mrkdwn",
        "text": "Deploy finished for <@U1234567890>. *v2.4.1* is live — <https://example.com/releases|release notes>"
      }
    },
    { "type": "divider" },
    {
      "type": "section",
      "fields": [
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Environment:*\nproduction" },
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Duration:*\n6m 12s" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "actions",
      "elements": [
        {
          "type": "button",
          "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Open dashboard" },
          "url": "https://example.com",
          "action_id": "open_dashboard"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Per-block rules to remember:

- `header` takes a single `text` of type `plain_text` only (no mrkdwn, no emoji rendering).
- `section` text may be `mrkdwn` or `plain_text`; `fields` render best two per row. Add an `accessory` (image/button) for compact side-by-side layouts.
- `context` holds small `mrkdwn`/`plain_text` lines and `image` elements — use it for metadata like timestamps or authors.
- `actions` holds buttons/selects/datepickers. Buttons with `value` + `action_id` require the app to handle interactions (Socket Mode / events); buttons with a `url` open links with no handler, which suits notification flows.
- Keep messages scannable: headline in a `header` or the first `section`, details below, action last.

## Anti-patterns

- Do not send a wall of `text` when a structured summary fits in a few blocks; Slack collapses long messages.
- Do not use `plain_text` where mrkdwn is intended (or vice versa).
- Do not invent IDs or dates; every mention, link label, and `<!date...>` fallback must resolve to something real or the message renders broken.

---
name: slack-api
description: "Send messages, ephemeral messages, thread replies, and reactions, upload files, and read conversations, users, and history through Slack's Web API and Incoming Webhooks. Use when a user asks to automate Slack notifications, query Slack workspace activity, or perform Slack actions with a bot token, user token, or webhook URL."
---

# Slack API

Use Slack's Web API (base URL https://slack.com/api/) and Incoming Webhooks to send and read workspace messages. The bundled script scripts/slack_request.cjs performs one authenticated request so the HTTP code does not get rewritten every time. For multi-step work (resolve an ID, then act, then page through results) call the script once per step.

## Credentials and identifiers

- Bot tokens start with xoxb-; user tokens start with xoxp-. Prefer a bot token with the smallest scope set that still works.
- Read tokens from environment variables (SLACK_TOKEN, SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL) or ask the user. Never hard-code a token in a file and never print a full token.
- Channel IDs start with C..., user IDs with U..., file IDs with F..., team IDs with T....
- A message timestamp (ts) such as 1700000000.123456 identifies a message and doubles as thread_ts for replies.

## Request helper

The helper needs Node.js 18+ and has no third-party dependencies. From the skill folder run:

    node scripts/slack_request.cjs --endpoint chat.postMessage --token "$SLACK_TOKEN" --payload '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello from a bot"}'

Send through an Incoming Webhook:

    node scripts/slack_request.cjs --webhook-url "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" --payload '{"text":"Hello"}'

Flags: --endpoint (Web API method; default chat.postMessage), --token, --webhook-url, --payload, --payload-file. The payload may also be piped on stdin. On success the script prints Success: followed by trimmed JSON (webhooks answer with plain text). On failure it prints a concise reason and exits non-zero: 1 means usage, transport, or HTTP error; 2 means Slack answered ok:false; 75 means rate limited (retry after the Retry-After seconds Slack reports).

## Common operations

Post a message: chat.postMessage with a channel ID and text. Add link_names: true to turn plain @name and #channel text into links; pass blocks for rich layouts. Plain text is preferred over attachments.

Reply in a thread: set thread_ts to the parent message ts. The response carries reply_ts so later replies can chain.

Send an ephemeral message: chat.postEphemeral with channel, user, and text; only that user sees it.

Update or delete a message: chat.update or chat.delete with channel and ts.

Resolve a channel name to an ID: conversations.list with types "public_channel,private_channel" and limit 1000, paging with cursor from response_metadata.next_cursor until the name matches. Needs channels:read and groups:read. When the app is already in the channel, conversations.info with the channel ID is cheaper.

Find a user: users.lookupByEmail with email (scope users:read.email), or page users.list with limit 1000. User IDs are stable; emails and display names are not.

Read history: conversations.history with channel and limit, plus optional oldest and latest (Unix seconds) to bound the window. Messages carry ts, user, text, and subtype for special kinds; page with next_cursor.

React to a message: reactions.add with channel, name (no colons), and timestamp; reactions.remove works the same way.

Search messages: search.messages with query (scope search:read).

Upload a file: files.upload is deprecated. Call files.getUploadURLExternal with filename and length to get upload_url and file_id, POST the raw bytes to upload_url (for example curl -F file=@report.csv "upload_url"), then call files.completeUploadExternal with files: [{"id":"F...","title":"report.csv"}]. Scope: files:write.

Open a modal: views.open with a view object and the trigger_id from an interaction.

## Message formatting

Slack uses mrkdwn: *bold*, _italic_, ~strikethrough~, and code spans wrapped in the single back-tick character. Mention a user with <@U123...>, reference a channel with <#C123...>, and hyperlink with <https://example.com|link text>. Set link_names: true to link plain @name and #channel text.

## Responses and errors

Web API responses set ok to true or false. Treat ok:false as a failure and surface the error string. Common errors:

- invalid_auth, not_authed, account_inactive: token wrong, revoked, or from a deleted app; ask for a fresh one.
- missing_scope: add the scope to the app and reinstall it in the workspace.
- channel_not_found: use the channel ID, not the name, and confirm the app is in the channel.
- not_in_channel: join public channels with conversations.join or ask an admin to invite the app.
- is_archived: pick a channel that is not archived.
- msg_too_long: text is limited to 40,000 characters; split the message or trim it.
- rate_limited: HTTP 429 with Retry-After; wait that many seconds and retry (the helper exits 75).

Pagination: methods return up to 100 to 1000 records per page (see the method docs) plus response_metadata.next_cursor. Keep paging while the cursor is non-empty and stop once the user's requested volume is reached.

Rate limits: roughly one request per second per method. Delay briefly between calls in a loop and always honor Retry-After on 429.

## Typical multi-step flow

1. Resolve targets first: look up channel and user IDs once and reuse them.
2. Perform the action with IDs.
3. Page only as far as needed and summarize counts instead of dumping full lists.
4. Report what was done: channel, message ts, and any failures.

## Scope checklist

---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack API. Send, schedule, update, delete, and thread messages; post to channels and DMs; list channels, members, and conversation history; manage reactions, files, and status; and compose messages with mrkdwn and Block Kit. Use when the user wants to automate Slack notifications, read from or write to a Slack workspace, or build Slack messages programmatically via the Web API or incoming webhooks.
---

# Slack API

Interact with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API (`https://slack.com/api/<method>`) or incoming webhooks. Covers notifications, reads, and message composition. Node 18+ is required for the bundled script.

## Authentication

- Export the token before calling the API: `export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-...` (bot token) or `xoxp-...` (user token). `scripts/slack_request.cjs` and the examples below read `SLACK_TOKEN`.
- Send it as `Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN`. Incoming webhook URLs carry their own auth; do not attach a token to them.
- Bots need the app installed in the destination channel (`chat:write`); to post to any public channel without joining it, add the `chat:write.public` scope.
- Never print tokens, commit them, or embed them in Slack message content. If a call fails with `invalid_auth`, `missing_scope`, `not_in_channel`, or `channel_not_found`, surface the exact error and fix auth/membership before retrying.

## API conventions

- POST to `https://slack.com/api/<method>` with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` (form-encoded bodies are also accepted; GET with query params works for reads). UTF-8 is required for non-ASCII text and emoji.
- Every response is an envelope: `{"ok": true, ...}` on success or `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` on failure. Always check `ok`; treat `ok: false` as an error and quote the `error` string. Slack often returns HTTP 200 for API-level failures.
- Prefer IDs over display names. Resolve them first via `conversations.list` / `users.list` — never invent IDs.
- Rate limits: on HTTP 429, back off for the seconds in the `Retry-After` header. The default tier is roughly 1 request/second per method, and list-type reads are stricter. Retry transient `internal_error` / `service_unavailable` responses with backoff.
- Pagination: paged responses return `response_metadata.next_cursor`; pass it back as `cursor` and repeat until empty.

## Quick start

Send a message with curl:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello from the build pipeline"}'
```

List channels (GET style) and read history (POST style):

```bash
curl -sS "https://slack.com/api/conversations.list?types=public_channel&limit=200" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN"
curl -sS -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.history \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SLACK_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"channel":"C1234567890","limit":10}'
```

Or use the bundled client `scripts/slack_request.cjs` — deterministic JSON handling, automatic 429/5xx retry, and LLM-friendly output:

```bash
node scripts/slack_request.cjs chat.postMessage '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello"}'
node scripts/slack_request.cjs conversations.list '{"types":"public_channel","limit":200}'
node scripts/slack_request.cjs conversations.history '{"channel":"C1234567890","limit":10}'
node scripts/slack_request.cjs users.lookupByEmail '{"email":"ada@example.com"}'
```

The script prints response JSON to stdout and exits `0` when `ok: true`, `1` on transport/HTTP failure, and `2` on usage/auth/config errors. If a method ever rejects a JSON body, fall back to curl with form fields: `curl -F channel=C1234567890 -F text=hi https://slack.com/api/chat.postMessage`.

## Task map

- Send a notification or message → `chat.postMessage`; reply in a thread by adding the parent message's `ts` as `thread_ts`.
- Message visible to only one user → `chat.postEphemeral`.
- Read channels / DMs / members / history / threads → `conversations.list`, `conversations.members`, `conversations.history`, `conversations.replies`.
- Create, rename, archive channels → `conversations.create`, `conversations.rename`, `conversations.archive`.
- Identify users → `users.list`, `users.info`, `users.lookupByEmail`.
- Set a status, react to a message, attach a file → `users.profile.set`, `reactions.add`, `files.upload`.

Endpoint details, arguments, and scopes: load `references/methods.md`. Before composing messages with formatting, mentions, links, dates, or interactive blocks: load `references/formatting.md`.

## Guardrails

- Resolve channel/user IDs through the API before sending; never fabricate them.
- Re-read content and destination before posting anything real, and stay within the user's stated intent; when the target channel is ambiguous, ask.
- When using `blocks`, always pass a short `text` fallback (used by notifications and accessibility tooling).
- Check `ok` in every response; a readable `error` string beats a generic failure.

# Slack Web API — Methods Reference

Load this file when a task needs argument details, scopes, or response shapes for specific methods. Confirm edge cases against `https://api.slack.com/methods/<method>` — exact scope requirements depend on the app's configuration and workspace settings.

Contents
- [Messaging](#messaging)
- [Conversations](#conversations)
- [Users](#users)
- [Reactions](#reactions)
- [Files](#files)
- [Incoming webhooks](#incoming-webhooks)
- [Common errors](#common-errors)

## Messaging

### chat.postMessage
Send a message to a channel, DM, or thread.

- `channel` (ID preferred), plus `text` and/or `blocks`. When using `blocks`, keep `text` as a short fallback for notifications.
- `thread_ts` replies inside the thread of an existing message.
- Optional: `mrkdwn`, `link_names` (linkify @names), `unfurl_links`, `unfurl_media`, `username`, `icon_emoji`.
- Scope: `chat:write` (bot must be a member of the channel, or the app has `chat:write.public` for public channels).
- Returns `channel`, `ts` (message id — reuse as `thread_ts` for replies), `message`.

### chat.postEphemeral
Message visible only to one `user` inside `channel`. Same body options as postMessage. Scope: `chat:write`.

### chat.update
Edit an existing message: `channel` + `ts`, with new `text`/`blocks`. Only messages created by the same token can be edited. Scope: `chat:write`.

### chat.delete
Delete a message: `channel` + `ts`. Scope: `chat:write`.

### chat.scheduleMessage
Schedule a message: `channel`, `text`/`blocks`, and `post_at` (unix timestamp; Slack allows up to 120 days in advance). Returns `scheduled_message_id`. Scope: `chat:write`.

## Conversations

### conversations.list
Enumerate conversations. `types` is a comma-separated list of `public_channel`, `private_channel`, `mpim`, `im` (defaults to `public_channel`). Use `limit`, `cursor`, `exclude_archived: true`. Scopes: `channels:read`, `groups:read`, `im:read`, `mpim:read`. Returns `channels[]` with `id`, `name`, `is_private`, `is_member`.

### conversations.info
Look up one conversation by `channel`. Same read scopes. Returns the conversation object including `purpose` and `topic`.

### conversations.history
Recent messages: `channel`, plus optional `limit`, `cursor`, `oldest`, `latest` (unix timestamps), `inclusive`. Scopes: `channels:history`, `groups:history`, `im:history`, `mpim:history`. Returns `messages[]`; each message has `ts`, `user`, `text`, and optional `blocks`, `thread_ts`, `reply_count`.

### conversations.replies
All messages in a thread: `channel` + `ts` of the parent message. Same history scopes. Returns the parent plus its replies.

### conversations.members
User IDs in a conversation: `channel`, plus `limit`/`cursor`. Read scopes as above. Resolve profiles separately with `users.info`, batching in small groups.

### conversations.create
Create a channel: `name` (no leading `#`, lowercase per Slack rules) and optional `is_private`. Scopes: `channels:manage` (public) / `groups:write` (private). Fails if a conversation with that name already exists.

### conversations.rename
Rename a conversation: `channel` + `name`. Scopes: `channels:manage` / `groups:write`.

### conversations.archive / unarchive
Archive or restore: `channel`. Scopes: `channels:manage` / `groups:write`. Posting to an archived channel fails with `is_archived`.

## Users

### users.list
List workspace members; paginate with `cursor`/`limit`. Scope: `users:read`. Can be slow in large workspaces — prefer `users.lookupByEmail` or `users.info` when you know the target.

### users.info
Profile for one user: `user`. Scope: `users:read`. Email is only returned when the token has `users:read.email` and workspace settings allow it.

### users.lookupByEmail
Resolve a user id from `email`. Scope: `users:read.email`.

### users.profile.set
Update profile fields, e.g. status:

```json
{"profile": {"status_text": "In a meeting", "status_emoji": ":calendar:", "status_expiration": 0}}
```

`status_expiration` is a unix timestamp; `0` means never expire. Clear a status with an empty `status_text`. Scope: `users.profile:write`.

## Reactions

### reactions.add
Add an emoji reaction to a message: `channel`, `name` (emoji shortcode without colons, e.g. `white_check_mark`), and `timestamp` (the message `ts`). Scope: `reactions:write`.

### reactions.remove
Remove a reaction added by the acting user: same arguments as add. Scope: `reactions:write`.

### reactions.get
List reactions on a message: `channel` + `timestamp`. Scope: `reactions:read`.

## Files

### files.upload (legacy)
Upload a file: `channels`, plus `content` (text) or an actual file via multipart form, `filename`, optional `initial_comment`. Scope: `files:write`. Legacy endpoint — for new code prefer the three-step flow `files.getUploadURLExternal` → PUT to the returned URL → `files.completeUploadExternal`.

## Incoming webhooks

- Purpose: post messages without a token; the webhook URL itself is the secret.
- POST JSON to the webhook URL: `{"text": "...", "blocks": [...]}` with optional `channel`, `username`, `icon_emoji` overrides.
- Responds with plain text `ok` on success; there is no response envelope and no read capability. Use the Web API for anything beyond fire-and-forget posting.

## Common errors

- `invalid_auth` — bad or revoked token.
- `missing_scope` — token lacks the required scope.
- `not_in_channel` — bot is not in the target channel (or needs `chat:write.public` for public channels).
- `channel_not_found` — bad channel ID or name.
- `is_archived` — posting to an archived channel.
- `invalid_blocks` / `invalid_arguments` — malformed payload; check the JSON structure.
- `too_many_requests` / HTTP 429 — rate limited; honor `Retry-After`.
- `internal_error` / `service_unavailable` — transient; retry with backoff.

# Formatting Slack Messages

Load this file before composing message `text` or Block Kit `blocks` payloads. Links and mentions require real IDs — resolve them through the API first.

## text vs blocks

- `text` — a plain string rendered as mrkdwn by default (`mrkdwn: true`). Good for simple messages.
- `blocks` — structured Block Kit JSON for rich messages (sections, dividers, buttons). When blocks are present, `text` becomes the fallback used by notifications and screen readers, so always include a short one.
- `plain_text` objects never render formatting; `mrkdwn` objects do.

## mrkdwn syntax

- `*bold*`, `_italic_`, `~strike~`, `` `code` ``, and `` ```preformatted``` `` for multi-line preformatted text.
- Emoji: `:wave:`, `:white_check_mark:`, etc.
- User mention: `<@U1234567890>`; channel link: `<#C1234567890|general>`.
- Broadcasts: `<!channel>`, `<!here>`, `<!everyone>`, or a user group `<!subteam^S1234567890|eng>`.
- Links: `<https://example.com|Click here>`. Bare URLs are auto-linked by Slack.
- Dates from a unix timestamp with a fallback: `<!date^1699999999^{date_long} at {time}|never>`. Available tokens: `{date}`, `{date_long}`, `{date_short}`, `{date_pretty}`, `{date_short_pretty}`, `{time}`, `{time_secs}`.
- Escape `&`, `<`, `>` as `&`, `<`, `>` whenever they should appear literally (always escape user-supplied input).

## Block Kit essentials

Common block types: `section`, `divider`, `header`, `context`, `actions`, `image`; `input` is for modals only. Slack enforces limits (e.g. max 50 blocks per message, ~3000 characters per block text object) — check https://api.slack.com/reference/block-kit/blocks before pushing anything close to the edge.

Full message payload example (sections, fields, divider, actions):

```json
{
  "channel": "C1234567890",
  "text": "Deploy finished: v2.4.1 is live",
  "blocks": [
    {
      "type": "section",
      "text": {
        "type": "mrkdwn",
        "text": "Deploy finished for <@U1234567890>. *v2.4.1* is live — <https://example.com/releases|release notes>"
      }
    },
    { "type": "divider" },
    {
      "type": "section",
      "fields": [
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Environment:*\nproduction" },
        { "type": "mrkdwn", "text": "*Duration:*\n6m 12s" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "type": "actions",
      "elements": [
        {
          "type": "button",
          "text": { "type": "plain_text", "text": "Open dashboard" },
          "url": "https://example.com",
          "action_id": "open_dashboard"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Per-block rules to remember:

- `header` takes a single `text` of type `plain_text` only (no mrkdwn, no emoji rendering).
- `section` text may be `mrkdwn` or `plain_text`; `fields` render best two per row. Add an `accessory` (image/button) for compact side-by-side layouts.
- `context` holds small `mrkdwn`/`plain_text` lines and `image` elements — use it for metadata like timestamps or authors.
- `actions` holds buttons/selects/datepickers. Buttons with `value` + `action_id` require the app to handle interactions (Socket Mode / events); buttons with a `url` open links with no handler, which suits notification flows.
- Keep messages scannable: headline in a `header` or the first `section`, details below, action last.

## Anti-patterns

- Do not send a wall of `text` when a structured summary fits in a few blocks; Slack collapses long messages.
- Do not use `plain_text` where mrkdwn is intended (or vice versa).
- Do not invent IDs or dates; every mention, link label, and `<!date...>` fallback must resolve to something real or the message renders broken.

---
name: slack-api
description: "Send messages, ephemeral messages, thread replies, and reactions, upload files, and read conversations, users, and history through Slack's Web API and Incoming Webhooks. Use when a user asks to automate Slack notifications, query Slack workspace activity, or perform Slack actions with a bot token, user token, or webhook URL."
---

# Slack API

Use Slack's Web API (base URL https://slack.com/api/) and Incoming Webhooks to send and read workspace messages. The bundled script scripts/slack_request.cjs performs one authenticated request so the HTTP code does not get rewritten every time. For multi-step work (resolve an ID, then act, then page through results) call the script once per step.

## Credentials and identifiers

- Bot tokens start with xoxb-; user tokens start with xoxp-. Prefer a bot token with the smallest scope set that still works.
- Read tokens from environment variables (SLACK_TOKEN, SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL) or ask the user. Never hard-code a token in a file and never print a full token.
- Channel IDs start with C..., user IDs with U..., file IDs with F..., team IDs with T....
- A message timestamp (ts) such as 1700000000.123456 identifies a message and doubles as thread_ts for replies.

## Request helper

The helper needs Node.js 18+ and has no third-party dependencies. From the skill folder run:

    node scripts/slack_request.cjs --endpoint chat.postMessage --token "$SLACK_TOKEN" --payload '{"channel":"C1234567890","text":"Hello from a bot"}'

Send through an Incoming Webhook:

    node scripts/slack_request.cjs --webhook-url "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL" --payload '{"text":"Hello"}'

Flags: --endpoint (Web API method; default chat.postMessage), --token, --webhook-url, --payload, --payload-file. The payload may also be piped on stdin. On success the script prints Success: followed by trimmed JSON (webhooks answer with plain text). On failure it prints a concise reason and exits non-zero: 1 means usage, transport, or HTTP error; 2 means Slack answered ok:false; 75 means rate limited (retry after the Retry-After seconds Slack reports).

## Common operations

Post a message: chat.postMessage with a channel ID and text. Add link_names: true to turn plain @name and #channel text into links; pass blocks for rich layouts. Plain text is preferred over attachments.

Reply in a thread: set thread_ts to the parent message ts. The response carries reply_ts so later replies can chain.

Send an ephemeral message: chat.postEphemeral with channel, user, and text; only that user sees it.

Update or delete a message: chat.update or chat.delete with channel and ts.

Resolve a channel name to an ID: conversations.list with types "public_channel,private_channel" and limit 1000, paging with cursor from response_metadata.next_cursor until the name matches. Needs channels:read and groups:read. When the app is already in the channel, conversations.info with the channel ID is cheaper.

Find a user: users.lookupByEmail with email (scope users:read.email), or page users.list with limit 1000. User IDs are stable; emails and display names are not.

Read history: conversations.history with channel and limit, plus optional oldest and latest (Unix seconds) to bound the window. Messages carry ts, user, text, and subtype for special kinds; page with next_cursor.

React to a message: reactions.add with channel, name (no colons), and timestamp; reactions.remove works the same way.

Search messages: search.messages with query (scope search:read).

Upload a file: files.upload is deprecated. Call files.getUploadURLExternal with filename and length to get upload_url and file_id, POST the raw bytes to upload_url (for example curl -F file=@report.csv "upload_url"), then call files.completeUploadExternal with files: [{"id":"F...","title":"report.csv"}]. Scope: files:write.

Open a modal: views.open with a view object and the trigger_id from an interaction.

## Message formatting

Slack uses mrkdwn: *bold*, _italic_, ~strikethrough~, and code spans wrapped in the single back-tick character. Mention a user with <@U123...>, reference a channel with <#C123...>, and hyperlink with <https://example.com|link text>. Set link_names: true to link plain @name and #channel text.

## Responses and errors

Web API responses set ok to true or false. Treat ok:false as a failure and surface the error string. Common errors:

- invalid_auth, not_authed, account_inactive: token wrong, revoked, or from a deleted app; ask for a fresh one.
- missing_scope: add the scope to the app and reinstall it in the workspace.
- channel_not_found: use the channel ID, not the name, and confirm the app is in the channel.
- not_in_channel: join public channels with conversations.join or ask an admin to invite the app.
- is_archived: pick a channel that is not archived.
- msg_too_long: text is limited to 40,000 characters; split the message or trim it.
- rate_limited: HTTP 429 with Retry-After; wait that many seconds and retry (the helper exits 75).

Pagination: methods return up to 100 to 1000 records per page (see the method docs) plus response_metadata.next_cursor. Keep paging while the cursor is non-empty and stop once the user's requested volume is reached.

Rate limits: roughly one request per second per method. Delay briefly between calls in a loop and always honor Retry-After on 429.

## Typical multi-step flow

1. Resolve targets first: look up channel and user IDs once and reuse them.
2. Perform the action with IDs.
3. Page only as far as needed and summarize counts instead of dumping full lists.
4. Report what was done: channel, message ts, and any failures.

## Scope checklist

chat:write to send, update, and delete messages; chat:write.customize for bot name and icon overrides; channels:read and groups:read for conversation metadata; im:read and mpim:read for DM and group history; users:read and users:read.email for member lookup; reactions:write; files:write for uploads; search:read for search.messages; incoming-webhook when using a webhook URL.
